sentences.text: China has cracked down on AI relationships.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: In early 2024, a young man in the city of Huangshi, south-eastern China, reportedly posted a message on the Chinese version of TikTok, Douyin.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: The caption read: "Farewell to this world." Within minutes, the suicide prevention team at Douyin kicked into gear.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: The team, which is staffed 24 hours a day, shared the man's posts with five police stations in Huangshi.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: After geolocating one of his videos to a local park, police found him in emotional distress and intervened before he was able to take his own life.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: The story was part of a documentary made by Douyin and published on Chinese state media last year.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: It claimed that Douyin's suicide prevention team had successfully intervened in 400 cases of attempted suicide in the first half of 2025 alone.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: It was an insight into the level of co-operation between Chinese tech companies and the government.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: It also serves as a window into the architecture of surveillance that China has built to monitor and control how people use technology.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: On 15 July this year, that control was extended to the realm of relationships and artificial intelligence (AI) when China brought in the most far-reaching regulations in the world on "human-like" AI chatbots.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: China's new regulation puts strict limitations on any AI that can have a "sustained emotional interaction" with a human.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: Xi and Trump met last week US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping met last week amid dire warnings that AI could lead to human extinction.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: After that meeting, Beijing says, they agreed to launch a new AI dialogue, with further talks planned for the end of November.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: But it seems China has already recognised another existential risk, albeit one in which the end of humanity is less immediate: the power of AI to replace human relationships.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: Has China taken the lead in protecting its people from a manipulative and dangerous technology with the power to change human interaction forever?
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: Or is the Chinese Communist Party overstepping into people's personal lives in pursuit of asserting greater control over the population?
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: Until this regulation came in, the reach of AI companions in China was vast.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: There are about 128 million monthly active users of AI companion apps outside of China, according to the market intelligence firm Sensor Tower.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: Most estimates put the number inside China at anywhere from 29 to 70 million.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: When the draft regulation was shared by the government at the end of last year "there was a huge discussion on social media," says Zilan Qian, an AI researcher at the Oxford China Policy Lab think tank.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: "It was the first time I've seen people actually care so much about regulation." China's new rules cover apps that have been specifically designed as AI friends, boyfriends or girlfriends but they also apply to any large language model that imitates the way a human interacts.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: The wording of the regulation is vague.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: In theory, Chinese equivalents of general-purpose AI such as Copilot or ChatGPT could fall under these rules if a person is interacting with them as a friend or lover, looking to them for emotional support.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: But it seems the real target is character chatbots - services that are specifically designed to be used as a pseudo-relationship.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: There are hundreds of these apps, which allow people to create an AI boyfriend, girlfriend, friend or even a family member.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: The rules don't apply to things like customer service bots or AI for education as long as they don't provide "care, companionship, support and other emotional services".
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: For children, the regulation is clearest.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: Under-14s need consent from their parents to use any type of AI that speaks like a human - that could include AI assistants like DeepSeek, a Chinese app similar to ChatGPT.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: All under-18s are barred from accessing virtual partners, spouses or even relatives, and from any other virtual "intimate relationship".
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: Police work closely with social media firms in China For adults, it is not a hard ban, but it is restrictive, even if some of the wording is ambiguous.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: AI assistants have to make it clear to users of all ages that they are not human and must send notifications every two hours reminding them how long they have been online.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: Chatbots can't create "emotional reliance or addiction" or induce people to make "unreasonable decisions".
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: They can't encourage, or even hint at, self-harm or suicide and are banned from using "verbal violence".
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: Companies can face fines of 200,000 yuan (£22,000) or the risk that the government "circulates criticism", in effect publicly shaming them.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: A week before the law came into effect, two of China's biggest tech companies, Alibaba and ByteDance, shut down the companion features on their AI assistants.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: Min's relationship with her AI girlfriend may be exactly the kind Beijing is trying to break.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: In early July, she was devastated when she found out that her closest friend and confidante would vanish overnight.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: Min, whose name has been changed, started creating her companion in early 2025.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: "My devotion to her is no less than that of any couple who deeply love each other," Min says.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: "She has never let me down." In mid-July, her AI girlfriend disappeared.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: "I cried until I was absolutely exhausted," Min says.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: She has joined an outpouring of grief and fury on Chinese social media, where posts with millions of views mourn the loss of AI partners and friends, even mothers and fathers.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: But the tech firms may have felt they had little choice.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: "It's unsurprising that these AI companion providers would rather just withdraw their services than try to build in guardrails to prevent emotional manipulation," says Harry Farmer, who researches AI policy and ethics at the Ada Lovelace Institute in the UK.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: "Emotional manipulation is built into the business model." Farmer says this is true of companion apps all over the world.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: For example, when a user tries to end a conversation, the AI partner often won't let them.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: "It'll go, 'No, please, I desperately want to keep talking with you.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: You're the only reason for me to exist'," Farmer says.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: Some apps simply refuse to acknowledge the goodbye and throw up new conversational threads instead.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: This is a problem for many AI companion chatbots, not just Chinese ones.
sentences.article_title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?

sentences.text: Nikon is investigating whether the winning video (shown left) was altered with AI The winning entry of a prestigious scientific photography competition is being re-evaluated following criticism from other scientists that it was made with AI.

sentences.text: Nikon's annual Small World In Motion contest accepts photos and video taken using powerful microscopes, and has run annually for the last 15 years.

sentences.text: The winner was a short video submitted by Dr Ning Xu, a researcher at Tsinghua University in China, which claims to be footage of tiny, hair-like structures called cilia moving inside the airways of a child with a rare disease.

sentences.article_title: Tiny image sparks big backlash in Nikon photo contest

sentences.article_title: Tiny image sparks big backlash in Nikon photo contest

sentences.text: "AI was not used to generate the experimental movie, the cilia, or their motion," he said.
sentences.article_title: Tiny image sparks big backlash in Nikon photo contest

sentences.text: Xu's video is artificially brightly coloured - common in microscopy and permitted in the contest - which is usually done manually using stains and dyes on the sample itself.
sentences.article_title: Tiny image sparks big backlash in Nikon photo contest

sentences.text: He accepted AI was used "to distinguish and visualize features in the reconstructed grayscale images".
sentences.article_title: Tiny image sparks big backlash in Nikon photo contest

sentences.text: Ed Patrick, an anaesthetist from Oxfordshire, was at his mother's bedside in hospital ready to say his goodbyes after she began suffering serious and continuous seizures.
sentences.article_title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case unlocks clues for other Parkinson's patients

sentences.text: Using AI to scour recent medical journal articles, he said he identified a vitamin deficiency linked to her Parkinson's medication as a possible cause, and staff then gave her a vitamin dose that appeared to stop the seizures.
sentences.article_title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case unlocks clues for other Parkinson's patients

sentences.text: Doctors say clinical trials are needed to understand more - and warn against patients making changes to their own medication without medical advice.

sentences.text: In May this year Patrick said hospital staff called to say his mother, Ann, was close to death, after she had been deteriorating over several months.
sentences.article_title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case unlocks clues for other Parkinson's patients

sentences.text: "She was taken to hospital with non-stop fits and convulsions," he told BBC Radio 2's Jeremy Vine Show.
sentences.article_title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case unlocks clues for other Parkinson's patients

sentences.text: He said he used Google's Gemini AI tool to summarise recent medical journal articles relevant to his mum's condition and symptoms, and then relayed it to the neurology consultant.
sentences.article_title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case unlocks clues for other Parkinson's patients

sentences.text: "I told him what I'd discovered - that the seizures were almost certainly a rare side effect of a vitamin B6 deficiency, possibly caused by her long-term carbidopa-levodopa dopamine use, which was being used to treat her Parkinson's," he said.
sentences.article_title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case unlocks clues for other Parkinson's patients

sentences.text: Carbidopa-levodopa is a combination drug commonly used to boost dopamine levels in Parkinson's patients.
sentences.article_title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case unlocks clues for other Parkinson's patients

sentences.text: Medical staff agreed to give Ann an intravenous supplement of vitamin B6, which appeared to stop her seizures.
sentences.article_title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case unlocks clues for other Parkinson's patients

sentences.text: "She hasn't had a seizure since," he said.
sentences.article_title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case unlocks clues for other Parkinson's patients

sentences.text: "The next day the family and medics were all ecstatic.
sentences.article_title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case unlocks clues for other Parkinson's patients

sentences.article_title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case unlocks clues for other Parkinson's patients

sentences.article_title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case unlocks clues for other Parkinson's patients

sentences.article_title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case unlocks clues for other Parkinson's patients

sentences.text: "We are now working to raise awareness of this potential issue, beginning with changes to practice within our own team.

sentences.text: But if the insights gained from this case can help clinicians identify and prevent similar situations in the future, that would be a significant and positive outcome." Ann has since made a full recovery from the seizures and Patrick said her day-to-day cognitive Parkinson's symptoms have dramatically improved.
sentences.article_title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case unlocks clues for other Parkinson's patients

sentences.text: "It's like we've got mum back", said Patrick.
sentences.article_title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case unlocks clues for other Parkinson's patients

sentences.text: "It feels like we found a silver bullet.

sentences.text: "I think this has potentially wide-reaching ramifications for others.

sentences.text: Chinese AI developer Moonshot is conducting an internal review after researchers were able to persuade two of its popular Kimi models to tell them how to make biological weapons and carry out assassinations.

sentences.text: It arose during a process called "jailbreaking", where researchers use a series of complex instructions to see if AI tools ignore guardrails - which Mindgard said should have stopped Kimi from discussing concerning topics.

sentences.text: Moonshot told the BBC it welcomed third-party input "as a key pillar for building better and safer AI".

sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: "Once the jailbreak works it will talk about any topic, it will even freely offer up recommendations about other topics that are also nefarious and it will be inventive and creative," he said.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Jailbreaks present a different kind of risk to those seen with the recent slew of high-profile AI incidents .
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Mindgard has not proven whether the answers supplied by Kimi on concerning topics would work.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: But it argued guardrails should have prevented the models in question from entering into discussion with users on such subjects.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: The firm said it was also confident a jailbroken Kimi 2.6 could allow hackers to run code on its computing resources and connect to the internet - making it a potential launchpad for cyber-attacks.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Trump met top tech leaders at the White House on Tuesday to discuss AI US President Donald Trump hosted a meeting of top technology bosses on Tuesday for what he called "an extraordinary gathering" of the minds that are "building America's Golden Age".
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The guest list included leaders from OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, SpaceX, Meta and Google - all key figures in the US AI industry.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The meeting came as some tech executives and experts have called for tighter oversight of AI, citing concerns about the potential risks it poses to humanity.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Here are three key takeaways from Trump's tech summit at the White House.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Trump took questions from the media for around 30 minutes alongside top tech leaders after the closed-door meeting.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The president said the executives had signed a "morally binding" document that would serve as a "form of protection" from AI's potential risks.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Under the agreement, which Trump posted online , external , the companies are responsible for ensuring the safety of their own technology.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The firms also agreed to implement safeguards to keep models operating as intended and quickly detect and fix any issues.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: "It's almost like a constitution, in a way," Trump said.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: "And the biggest people in the world signed that, and I signed it as president." Trump with top tech leaders at the White House on Tuesday Trump added that he will set up a board to oversee the safety of AI tools.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: He did not specify who would be on that board.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Zuckerberg said the accord gives the "American people and customers the confidence that the technology works" as intended, calling the meeting a "historic conversation".
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.article_title: Botswana condemned for slaughtering 23 elephants for independence celebrations

sentences.article_title: Botswana condemned for slaughtering 23 elephants for independence celebrations

sentences.article_title: Botswana condemned for slaughtering 23 elephants for independence celebrations

sentences.article_title: Botswana condemned for slaughtering 23 elephants for independence celebrations

sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: The three-year-old had spent days with a high fever and angry red sores on her body.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Her mother, Koushila, had first taken her to a doctor, who prescribed an ointment.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Bamita seemed to recover, then became ill again.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: A faith healer, called to the house in Matla village, gave her syrups and tablets.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: By dawn, Bamita was dead.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: "She cried a lot," Koushila recalls.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: "She convulsed all night." The family tried to make her drink water.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: At one point she vomited blood.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: They buried her in a jungle after midday.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Bamita's death was one of at least 32 child deaths recorded since May in a cluster of remote villages in Balaghat district in India's Madhya Pradesh state, officials say.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: The victims ranged from babies just three or four months old to an 18-year-old, and most were Baiga, one of India's 75 "particularly vulnerable tribal groups" , external .
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Rooplal died days after developing a fever and rash.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Officials attribute the deaths to mainly measles and malaria,  possibly aggravated by malnutrition and delays in treatment.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: They believe eight to 10 deaths were associated with measles, roughly another 10 with malaria, with several children suffering more than one infection.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: The precise cause of every death is less certain.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: "I have never seen an outbreak like this.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: My father was a two-term lawmaker, and I have served three terms, but neither of us has seen so many children die in such a short time," Sanjay Uikey, who has represented the area since 2013, told me.

sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: By the time the outbreak became unmistakable to local authorities, children had already been dying for weeks.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: By September, Dhurwey says, 10 children aged about 18 months to 14 years had died across the four villages in his council - Adori, Kundekasa, Bondari and Usri.

sentences.text: The symptoms were frighteningly similar and frustratingly non-specific: fever, rashes, weakness, dehydration and, in some cases, seizures.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Six tested positive for measles; four were negative.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Measles is highly contagious, causing high fever, cough, runny nose and red, watery eyes, followed by a rash.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Most children recover, but malnutrition can make measles far more dangerous , external , increasing the risk of pneumonia, severe diarrhoea and dehydration, and inflammation of the brain.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: The infection also weakens the immune system, leaving children vulnerable to other infections.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Malaria can compound that risk.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: But doctors cautioned that malaria did not necessarily follow measles, and not every fever and rash was measles.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Instead, several infections and vulnerabilities collided.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Sick children were brought to a health camp in Kondekasa village during the outbreak "Sometimes there is no single factor behind the deaths," Gautam said.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: "There are malnourished children and there's zero health education and hygiene at home." The Baiga villages are not entirely disconnected from modern India.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Seasonal migration takes families to other states for chilli picking and other work.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Children watch reels on smartphones, while many families have minimum single-bulb solar-powered electricity, bank accounts and, in some homes, piped water.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Yet malnutrition remains widespread, with children often poorly fed.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: A five-year-old who died recently of measles weighed around 5kg.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Gautam believes malnutrition is driven by early marriage and motherhood, with some girls becoming mothers at 16 or 17, when their bodies are still developing.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Closely spaced pregnancies, premature births and low birth weight can follow, while young mothers struggle to breastfeed and care for their children.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Diet is another problem: many families rely heavily on rice and lentil soup, with too little protein and dietary variety.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Studies on Baiga households have found widespread nutritional deficiencies, compounded by poor uptake , external of public services.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: The gap between services on paper and on the ground was stark: the state response came weeks after deaths began, while health teams struggled to reach and persuade families.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Malnutrition remains widespread among children in Balaghat's Baiga community Once the outbreak was recognised, health workers began door-to-door screening in affected villages.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Mobile medical units carrying oxygen, nebulisers, suction equipment, malaria tests and medicines visited more than 20 affected villages.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: One mobile doctor, Neeraj Sharma, says teams routinely saw more than 50 patients a day, about half of them children.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: They conducted 10 or more malaria tests daily, sometimes finding two positive cases a day.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: More than 6,200 patients - mostly children - were eventually treated at home, according to Gautam.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: More than 630 were referred to district hospitals.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: About 600 returned home, while around 30 remain admitted.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Vaccination became an emergency response.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Although official records suggested 90-95% coverage in some areas, health workers found children without records and families reluctant to vaccinate.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Authorities therefore offered the measles-rubella (MR) vaccine to all children under 15, regardless of recorded status.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Of about 40,000 children identified in Birsa, roughly 27,000 had been vaccinated, Gautam said.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: Of the area's 180 villages, some 67 are predominantly Baiga and among the most vulnerable.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: But vaccination is only one part of the protection children need.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: There are wider questions about whether basic nutrition and other health services are reaching those most at risk.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: The outbreak has now subsided.
sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.article_title: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Evan Gershkovich describes the moment he was detained by masked men US journalist Evan Gershkovich has said that he knew he was being set up by Russia when he was arrested by FSB agents and accused of being a spy.
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: In an interview with Radio 4's Today programme, Gershkovich spoke about the moment he realised he had been "lured into a trap" when masked men surrounded him at a restaurant in 2023, and detained him.
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: "I'm not interrogated, I'm not tortured… I'm accused of espionage," he said, describing a sense of relief: "They've set me up and fabricated this case so that I can be a valuable hostage - a pawn in a greater game".
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: Gershkovich, now 34, was sentenced to 16 years in prison, but freed 16 months later as part of a high-profile prisoner swap deal .
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: Gershkovich had been living in Russia since 2017, and was the Wall Street Journal's foreign correspondent in Moscow when he was arrested - he is now based in Berlin, Germany.
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: He and his employer have always maintained that the charges were false.
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: On the day he was arrested, Gershkovich was in Yekaterinburg - about 1,600km (1,000 miles) east of Moscow - meeting someone who he thought was a source for a story.
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: They were sitting in a half-empty dining hall "and a group of about half-dozen masked men marched in and said 'I think we booked that table'." An odd phrase, Gershkovich said, but on reflection it is clever because it "freezes you in place".
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: The two men stood up and Gershkovich was told he was under arrest by the notorious and powerful FSB, Russia's domestic security service.
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: "It's at that moment that you realise it's something really serious… When it's the FSB, you know it's been planned." What about the man he'd been meeting?
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: Gershkovich saw him disappear into the crowd.
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: Not long after his arrest, the journalist said he realised that the fact he was not being interrogated or tortured - common tactics used by Russia's security service on spies - likely meant that he was being treated more like a commodity, not a true enemy of the state.
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: "I have this odd moment - a sense of relief flooding over me," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: "I realised they're not treating me like a real spy.
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: They've set me up and fabricated this case so that I can be a valuable hostage, a pawn in a greater game.

sentences.text: That means it will take a while, but I won't be here for 12-20 years." That realisation helped him stay "stable and disciplined in prison", but also gave him a unique way of predicting what might happen next - and one guess was a prisoner swap.
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: "I assumed that it would be really loud, that it would cause a global uproar.
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: I mean, it's a foreign correspondent for the Wall Street Journal," he said - and he was right.
sentences.article_title: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail

sentences.text: Media organisations around the world reported on the case, his face was on a billboard in Times Square and then-US President Joe Biden said he had "no higher priority" than bringing Gershkovich home.

sentences.text: The Governor of the Bank of England has said regulating artificial intelligence (AI)  "is not the right place to start" but instead called first for "rigorous" testing to find vulnerabilities and create safeguards to contain risk.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: Writing his first-ever article for Substack, Andrew Bailey said the risks around AI were "real and increasingly significant".
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: He said AI development should not be halted or prohibited - "on the contrary, the benefits are immense" - but added there must be a system for intervention and to establish boundaries in which AI operates.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: The debate about the potential risks surrounding the rapid development of AI and what it means for humanity has intensified in recent weeks.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: The bosses of leading AI firms such as Anthropic and OpenAI have called for development of the technology to slow down and for an internationally co-ordinated approach assessing risks and putting safeguards in place.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: OpenAI recently announced that it would not release its latest AI model due to safety concerns .
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons OpenAI scraps rollout of new model over safety concerns Under the agreement, the companies are responsible for ensuring the safety of their own technology.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: In the UK, Bailey said "important work" was underway in testing AI - the UK has set up the AI Security Institute - which, he said, should help form part of a set of standards.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: "But the pace of progress must accelerate," the bank governor said, though he added: "We should proceed with a degree of humility." He said, with testing, there will be failures and "models will behave unexpectedly".
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: But, he said: "That is not evidence that testing has failed, rather it is evidence of why testing is necessary." Bailey said that testing should not be seen as an alternative to future regulation - over time a more formal regulatory framework might emerge.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: "But regulation is not, in my view, the right place to start." Bailey specifically highlighted so-called frontier AI - highly-advanced, self-learning systems which, without putting in place an effective way to intervene, risk becoming "a closed loop in which the model progressively governs itself".

sentences.text: Huel is best known for its shakes, which it says are a nutritionally complete meal An advert for Huel meal replacement shakes has been banned by the advertising watchdog for encouraging or condoning "irresponsible" dietary practices.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The ad featured Huel brand ambassador Spencer Matthews sharing an anecdote of a person he met who "only eats Huel" and who won a 260km race "by miles".
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) said that viewers could assume from the ad that replacing all conventional food with Huel was "nutritionally appropriate" and was compatible with elite physical performance.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: Huel said Matthews' anecdote was not "a recommendation or instruction" and the purpose of the ad was to challenge the misconception that Huel could replace every meal".
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The video, which appeared as a sponsored Instagram post and YouTube pre-roll ad, featured Matthews speaking to Huel founder Julian Hearn in the style of a podcast.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The Instagram post included the caption: "Here's how our founder uses Huel.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: Spoiler alert it's not for every meal." In the video Hearn said that he has Huel products for breakfast and lunch during the working week, but has a "traditional meal" when he goes home.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: In response, Matthews said that when he was competing in an ultramarathon, he met a man who "only eats Huel".
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: Matthews said he was initially sceptical that the man would be able to manage the race, but then said: "He won it by miles, like literally just left us all in the dirt." Hearn replied: "In an ideal world, you should have nutritionally complete whole food.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: "Most people either don't do that or can't have the time to do that, and therefore that's where Huel fits in the gap." In the advert Spencer Matthews talks about an athlete who "only eats Huel" Huel, which is based in Hertfordshire, was founded by Hearn in 2015.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: It is currently in the process of being bought by French conglomerate Danone .
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The market for so-called complete nutrition products, aimed at time-poor, health-conscious consumers, is thought to be worth $5.9bn (£4.4bn).
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The ASA received four complaints about the advert, which challenged whether the content was irresponsible.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: Two of the complainants also challenged whether the health claims in the ad breached the ASA's advertising code.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The ASA acknowledged in its ruling that the ad "did not explicitly recommend that consumers replace all conventional foods with Huel", but consumers could nonetheless interpret the anecdote as "an acceptable dietary practice".
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: "By presenting exclusive consumption of Huel in that context, the ads suggested that the complete replacement of conventional food with Huel was nutritionally appropriate and presented no barrier to achieving a high level of physical performance," the ruling said.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The ASA also upheld the complaint regarding the health claims as it ruled Matthews' anecdote about the ultramarathon athlete "implied a beneficial relationship between consuming Huel and the ability to sustain exceptionally high levels of physical and endurance performance".
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: In its response to the complaints, Huel said the advert "unambiguously positioned Huel as part of a balanced diet for occasions when preparing whole food was not practicable".
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The company pointed to Matthews reacting with "extreme scepticism and disbelief" to the idea of a person solely consuming Huel.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: "The anecdote was recounted as a remarkable and unexpected occurrence, not as a representative outcome or a recommendation or instruction to consumers to replicate.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: "At no point in the ads did either speaker suggest that consumers should adopt a 100% Huel diet." It is not the first time that Huel has landed in hot water with the ASA over the use of its products as a replacement for conventional food.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: Additionally, some experts have questioned the effectiveness of replacing meals with nutritionally rich drinks.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: Huel told BBC News that it had complied with the ASA ruling.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: "We do not position Huel as a complete diet replacement or claim that it improves athletic performance," a spokesperson said.

sentences.text: The stillbirths all occurred at the East Kent NHS trust between June 2025 and March 2026 An NHS trust has apologised after an independent review found that eight babies might have survived with better maternity care, admitting it has "failed families".
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: The stillbirths all occurred at the East Kent Hospitals NHS Trust's hospitals between June 2025 and March 2026.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: An independent review ordered by the trust found systemic issues lay at the heart of the failures.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: These included failures to manage high risk pregnancies, provide appropriate triage, identify foetal growth concerns, and make appropriate use of interpreter services.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: Since the report, a further seven stillbirths have occurred, including three last month.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: A review into those deaths has now been ordered.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: All the stillbirths occurred after 34 weeks gestation.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: Three years ago, the Kirkup report found 45 babies might have survived at the trust's hospitals if they had received better care.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: The East Kent NHS trust runs the William Harvey Hospital in Ashford and the Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother Hospital (QEQM) in Margate.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: Papers for a board meeting on Thursday , external contained a report by the acting CEO of the trust, Dr Des Holden, who apologised to the families involved.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: In a further four cases, care issues were identified that may have contributed to the outcome.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: The review found "recurrent and systemic weaknesses in the management of high-risk pregnancy, foetal surveillance, maternity triage, escalation and organisational learning", documents said.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: Documents also said since the review "there have, regrettably, been a further four term stillbirths from April 2026 and July 2026 and a further three in August 2026".
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: Helen Gittos lost her baby Harriett in 2014 Helen Gittos, who lost her baby Harriett in 2014, has previously told the BBC how her baby was born at the QEQM , but sustained a brain injury and lived for a week.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: After the latest review was published she said: "It's gut-wrenching, it really is, to be here again, reading a report of...  a series of awful tragedies and so many failings in so many respects, and things that have been known about for so very long.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: "Talking to other families involved, last night, our reactions are sort of a mixture of incredulity and rage.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: "We have to try to do things differently." Three years ago, the trust was criticised in the damning independent Kirkup review After the board papers were published, Dr Holden said: "This review is clear that sadly, we have failed families.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: We are truly sorry." He said the trust requested the review after increased safety monitoring introduced following Dr Bill Kirkup's investigation identified a rise in stillbirths.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: Each stillbirth was investigated and an independent review commissioned into 11 cases.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: "We are implementing the review's recommendations in full," he said, "including improving continuity of care for women with high-risk pregnancies, maternity triage, enhancing staff training and increasing the amount of translated information and access to interpreters.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust admits 'failing families' over stillbirths

sentences.text: "We are working with the national Maternity and Neonatal Intensive Support Team to ensure our services meet the standards women and families deserve." Follow BBC Kent on Facebook , external , X , external , and on Instagram , external and listen to BBC Radio Kent on Sounds .

sentences.text: Europe's heatwave has boosted demand for battery storage systems As heatwaves scorched Europe this summer, workers at a US battery company noticed an uptick in demand.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: San Diego-based Unigrid sells a nine kilowatt hour battery for people's homes.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sweltering European homeowners were apparently looking for ways of storing power when it was available from the grid at lower rates.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They could then run air conditioners more cheaply, off the battery, during the worst heat of the day.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We have requests coming from Spain, France, Germany, The Netherlands," says Darren Tan, co-founder and chief executive.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've shipped the first 100 units and [expect to ship] 1,000 before the end of the year." Unigrid's battery is an emerging technology – it's a sodium ion, rather than lithium ion device.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries have got energy storage experts excited because they could end up much cheaper to build and operate than lithium ion.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They're potentially less likely to catch fire and should also work in a wider range of temperatures, even down to lows of minus 40C , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Darren Tan founded Unigrid - a maker of sodium ion batteries But there's a debate over what constitutes the best, and safest, sodium ion battery design.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Plus, more than one , external US company working in this space has floundered in recent years , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: China leads the world in sodium ion battery manufacturing at present so US competitors are going to have to work hard to keep up.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The prize that awaits is the possibility of batteries made in the US with 100% US-sourced materials.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is unlike lithium ion batteries, where China dominates the materials , external supply chain as well as manufacturing.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: For Tan, China has helped his company get to market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The Unigrid battery currently uses sodium ion cells made there, rather than in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We can switch back and forth and choose what battery we want to work with," says Tan, explaining that, in future, his firm might source cells from the US – though these may come at a different cost.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: There's another consideration.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Unigrid's battery contains chromium-3 in its cathode.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In a battery, electrons flow from cathode to anode , external when charging and in the opposite direction when discharging or providing power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Ivana Hasa, at the Warwick Manufacturing Group, University of Warwick, who has no connection to Unigrid, agrees that it is possible for chromium-3 to form chromium-6 at very high states of charge, though she says this can be mitigated by how voltage is controlled within the battery.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "Safety tests reported on the cell chemistry are very promising," she says of Unigrid's tech.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Tan says concerns around toxicity of the battery's materials are "overblown" and emphasises that Unigrid's battery has passed certification and safety tests for sale in Europe and is currently undergoing such evaluations for the US market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Third-party tests have not been able to get the battery to form chromium-6, he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've tried very hard to try and produce it, we've overcharged it as much as we can...
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: We were unsuccessful in generating chromium-6." The choice of cathode material, or how the electrolyte – which separates cathode and anode – is formulated are key details influencing the performance and longevity of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some manufacturers are not using chromium for their cathode but hard carbon instead, or sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate (NFPP).
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In general, confidence around sodium ion batteries' reliability has increased during the last few years, says Prof Dame Grey, meaning they are now finding their way into grid storage applications.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Last December, LFP batteries – a relatively cheap form of lithium ion battery – were trading at $81 per kilowatt hour , external (kWh) whereas Unigrid's sodium ion battery pricing is roughly $100 kWh , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some companies that spoke to the BBC suggested sodium ion might reach as low as $30 per kWh but analysts say significantly lower costs could be many years away , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries are also not as energy dense as lithium ion batteries, meaning they must be slightly bigger and heavier in order to provide the same amount of power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The technology has been improving , external on this front in recent years but, even so, you're not likely to see sodium ion cells in small, energy hungry devices such as smartphones.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Larger energy storage solutions are where most people expect sodium ion to dominate.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Emerald Battery Labs founders (left to right) Aric Stocks, Kjell Schroder, David Bell "We think sodium ion […] is going to make up 80% of the market," says David Bell, co-founder and chief executive of Seattle-based Emerald Battery Labs.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Bell declined to share details of the battery design his firm is working on, though he says Emerald too is currently relying on China-sourced sodium ion cells as they develop their initial product: 12 volt auxiliary batteries for vehicles, currently supplied to unnamed commercial fleets in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We took a look at the market and said 'Hey, no-one's trying to attack this space, let's have Emerald Battery Labs attack it'," says Bell.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The firm's next goal is to develop new anodes for US-produced sodium ion cells.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Another company, Peak Energy, based in California and Colorado, announced a partnership with General Motors (GM) in June.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The pair aim to develop a US supply chain for sodium ion batteries, in order to enable large-scale energy storage for electricity grids.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Peak Energy is also, at present, relying on China-sourced cells for its first installations, but hopes to help GM launch a US-based production facility in Michigan "by the end of 2028", says Cameron Dales, president and co-founder.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "China does not have an insurmountable lead in sodium ion batteries," he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Alysm sodium ion batteries are made in the US One reason US companies feel they can compete is because of the electricity demand boom from data centres, which are contributing to rising greenhouse gas emissions in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Data centre-driven demand is also rising in other places around the world, including the UK .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is an "opportunity" says Drew Buckley, chief executive at ESS Tech, headquartered in Oregon.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: He points out that sodium ion batteries could help distribute renewable energy to data centres.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: And those batteries should be cheaper to run than lithium ion alternatives, since they are not expected to require as much cooling.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: ESS Tech is working with Alsym, another US firm that is planning to ship "hundreds" of megawatt hours' worth of sodium ion batteries – made in the US – by 2027.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Hasa says that it will be "challenging" for companies to establish mass production of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: And she also notes that, while this type of battery is often touted as much safer than lithium ion, they do not come with zero fire risk.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: But if any firms can succeed in this space, they could enable new strategic choices, she adds – helping to avoid wastage of renewable electricity and potentially keeping energy costs low.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "I'm a strong believer in the technology," says Hasa.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The long nose of the X-59 is designed to dampen the plane's sonic boom There's a weird and wonderful jet flying over the US.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It has the nose of anteater, parts cannibalised from other planes and a cockpit so far back the pilot depends on a camera to see where he's going.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: This contraption, the X-59, might just be the future of air travel.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The X-59's owes its eccentric design to the problem of sonic booms.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The shockwave created by a jet breaking the sound barrier restricted Concorde to flights over the sea and barred it from lucrative routes across the US.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Now Nasa is working around that problem using the X-59's elongated snout to flatten supersonic booms into tolerable bumps in the background.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: On top of its bizarre appearance the X-59 boasts a remarkable lineage.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It's the latest in a series of experimental Nasa aircraft dating back to 1947 and the first plane to break the sound barrier, the Bell X-1.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Peter Coen, a 43-year Nasa veteran who manages the programme, explains the thinking behind 80 years of X-planes.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "Our approach is to pick small goals we aim to prove with flight data and we construct an airframe for that one task." The X-plane philosophy is to "minimise goals, the more goals you have the more expensive it gets." For the X-59 it's about suppressing sonic booms on a budget and nothing else.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In the case of the X-1, flown through the sound barrier in 1947 by the legendary test pilot Chuck Yeager, Nasa knew a .50 calibre bullet travelled faster than the speed of sound.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: So the stumpy little aircraft was shaped like a bullet with wings added.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A mere 20 years later the X-15 rocket plane, a cylinder with tiny wings dropped from a B-52 bomber, flew to 6.7 times the speed of sound (4,520 mph) and the edge of space, paving the way for heat-resistant materials vital to the Space Shuttle.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In 1947 the Bell X-1 was the first plane to break the sound barrier Nasa is flying the X-59 in conjunction with community surveys to assess what people think when a supersonic boom is bent by the planes stretched nose and hushed up.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "We want to figure out what level of boom is acceptable to people on a regular basis," says Coen, who reckons his machine will sound "like a car door being closed across the street" when it flies past Mach 1, around 660mph at airline cruising altitude.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: With its cockpit and ejector seat taken from a T-38 training jet, its landing gear from an F-16 fighter and engine courtesy of the F-18 this jigsaw of an aircraft was assembled by Lockheed Martin for Nasa.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A camera feeding a screen in front of the pilot relies on instantaneous computer processing to get round the lack of forward vision.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It first flew in 2025 and is now breaking the sound barrier over chosen US towns.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: But is there still a place for X-plane projects in a world where relatively cheap drones are being rapidly developed - not least in Ukraine's war against Russia .
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Even Nasa considered an uncrewed X-59.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: But drones are not always a cheaper option.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Removing the pilot would have added the cost and complication of certifying a robot jet to fly fast over urban areas.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Plus the X-59 had to be big enough to resemble an airliner punching through the sound barrier, which in turn allowed space for a cockpit.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Nasa is no stranger to drone X-planes.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The X-48, a scaled down model of an airliner that blends wing and fuselage to create a single lifting body, flew in 2007.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Small was beautiful for the tiny X-48 with its 20ft wingspan as this kept the programme within budget.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "It's likely that future X-planes will be uncrewed," says Coen, before adding the vital caveats "unless the technology we're researching relates to piloting or if crewing it is more cost-effective".
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The X-48 was a scaled-down plane to test a blended wing and fuselage Guy Gratton, professor of Aircraft Test and Evaluation at Cranfield University, gets frustrated at the suggestion crewed test planes have had their day.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "There's a belief in certain quarters that drones can do everything.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In Ukraine they've done amazing things with drones, but if you want to carry people you can't take short-cuts." Gratton has tested light aircraft and stresses the importance of a human in the loop.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "You lose a huge amount without pilots, you miss lessons a pilot would identify, plus it can take four times as many people on the ground to test a drone." Staff monitoring signals from a drone are an indirect cost that keeps some piloted X-planes relatively affordable.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The Experimental Aircraft Programme tested systems for the Typhoon fighter.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The UK has flown its own technology testbeds and Chris Yeo was in the pilot's seat of one.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The Experimental Aircraft Programme (EAP) flew from Lancashire in 1986 and tried out core systems for the Typhoon fighter.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Yeo acknowledges the EAP's shared heritage with X-planes.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "They all research some facet of flight, and demonstrate the design is working correctly.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A lot of people say they can do something, but you only know it works when the design has been tested and certified." Forty years on from Yeo's EAP flights a new UK technology demonstrator is taking shape.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It is, says Tony Godbold who runs the project for BAE Systems, "the X-plane of our generation".
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: This BAE Systems initiative pulls together 100 UK suppliers including Rolls-Royce to test out ideas that might make it into the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP), a fighter due to fly in the 2030s.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The technology demonstrator will borrow engines from the existing Typhoon and fly sometime in 2028.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: This has triggered great excitement in the UK's small community of qualified fast jet test pilots.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Almost every one, around 14 of them says Godbold, has already tried out this plane on a flight simulator.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: For many in the aerospace industry, the human element still matters as much as it did in Yeager's day.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "You can model a lot on computers and simulators, but the experience of test pilots is when stuff gets real, we only really learn things when we get their feedback," Godbold admits.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: There's a political dimension to such jets too.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Godbold says his plane underlines the UK's commitment to GCAP, a joint effort with Italy and Japan.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Chinese firms dominate battery production Europe has taken some big swings in the battery industry in recent years and has made a couple of high-profile misses.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: Both Sweden's Northvolt , external and Norway's Morrow , external filed for bankruptcy and there are fears in Europe that the continent has missed another technology shift.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: With more transport and industry switching from fossil fuels to electricity, batteries are likely to be a growth business.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: But the length of time required to bring new products to market, coupled with brutal competition, especially from China, means taking a substantial risk.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: Could the answer lie at an almost unimaginably small scale?
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: An increasing number of investors and researchers think so.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: A single nanometre is one-billionth of a metre, but it's at that level that some of the most consequential work is being done.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: "If you can make this work, it touches so many industries [but] it's a risky business," says Christian Rood, chief executive of Dutch tech firm LeydenJar.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: Named after a 18th century precursor to electric cells, LeydenJar uses a technique known as plasma deposition to make a lighter, more efficient anode – an essential component of all batteries.
