sentences.text: This video can not be played Freddo the robot in action at Vsim Freddo the robot walks across the office and takes a plastic bottle offered by a staff member.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Given that a robot recently beat Usain Bolt's 100m sprint record, it's not the most startling achievement.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But the speed by which Freddo has been trained to walk, recognise the bottle and grasp it is impressive.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It took just a few minutes to develop those skills and upload them to Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: His developers say rival systems could take days to attain such skills.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: I'm at Vsim, a British start-up based in Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey hope one day their software will control robots that can navigate and do useful tasks in the home and workplace.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But there's a long way to go.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It's a weird situation with robotics because actually the stuff that we find as humans to be incredibly difficult, like gymnastics, you can get robots to do reasonably well.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The stuff that humans are really good at, like fine dexterity, is really hard in robots," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Vsim founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey Freddo's skills were honed in a virtual environment, where a task can be performed  in a computer simulation millions of times.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Once the optimum solution (known as a policy) is found, it can be uploaded and used by the hardware - in this case Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Such virtual simulations are a common way to train robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Tech giant Nvidia has a system called Isaac Sim which works that way - Lu and Storey both worked on an early version of it.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: In 2022 they decided to set up Vsim, to build the their own training system environment and other tools.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: As they were starting from scratch Lu and Storey could optimise the software to exploit the powerful computer chips used in AI, known as graphics processing units or GPUs.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "The underlying algorithms that we were using for most of these robotic simulations they hark back to the 1970s and 1980s, but those algorithms are not really brilliant fits for GPUs," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Within months they realised their system could work much faster than anything they had seen before.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Eighteen months in and we actually have a completely functional, super high-performance simulator," says Lu.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The software is so efficient that it can run on the hardware carried by Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That means the robot can run tens of thousand of simulations while it is moving around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It can look about a second, or so, ahead into the future for 20,000 different kind of combinations of things that might happen," Storey explains.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And that would be vital for a robot moving around an unstructured environment like the average home.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Things outside of the robot's control, like humans, animals or even other robots, could do things that require a change of strategy.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: These unexpected events could happen very quickly and the robot needs to be able to quickly adapt to ensure its actions remain safe and on-mission," Lu says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Robot training systems use virtual environments where tasks are practised Vsim is a start-up with 10 engineers working on its tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Nvidia is at the other end of the industry.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It dominates the market for computer chips used for AI and has a leading robotics software division, with hundreds of engineers.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It does not build robots, instead it has a suite of software designed to let organisations train and control robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That includes virtual simulation training systems and a so-called world model , external , called Cosmos, which gives a robot an understanding of the physics of the real world and how its environment might change as it moves around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But even with the powerful computer resources available to Nvidia, the software only gives a rudimentary understanding of the real world.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Manipulation, - where I just grab a bottle, that's not too hard.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The problem is when you start doing long-horizon tasks, where I say: 'I want you to take the bottle and I want you to fill it up and I want you to go pour'," says Spencer Huang, director of product for robotics at Nvidia.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But he's confident that good progress is being made.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: This year Nvidia has started using AI agents to help build virtual environments to train robots and validate whether the solutions from training work or not.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "When we talk about creating the [virtual] world and actually scanning it in - a lot of that is actually manual labour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "We're just throwing agents at it... it's basically given us a huge workforce," Huang says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Simulation is not the only method for training robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: They can also be trained by watching human or video demonstrations.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Rika Antonova has spent more than a decade working in robotics Rika Antonova has been working in the field of robotics since 2015 and is currently an associate professor at the Department of Computer Science and Technology at the University of Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Her research is focused on , external developing software and hardware that can aid robots to learn complex behaviour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Antonova works with a training system called MuJoCo, owned by Google's DeepMind since 2021.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's open-source software, which means researchers can use it for free, and are allowed to tinker with the code.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It is very, very user-friendly.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: So for research groups or for small start-ups, that's useful," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: She says that Vsim's approach - very fast simulation - is promising.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "If you have a very, very fast simulator, then you can simulate hundreds of millions of samples in that few seconds that your robot is thinking about how to adjust its motion, and then you can change the motion almost in real time," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But those simulated environments are still rough approximations of the real world, which limits what can be trained.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "There are certain things that are hard to model in simulation, like highly deformable objects and cutting," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's a challenge that Nvidia and Lu and Storey at Vsim are working on.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says their system has "reduced approximation, using accurate simulations to train models that genuinely work in reality as well as they do in simulations." Soon a second robot, to be called Nacho, will be helping develop that tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says that should speed up their development process and ensure their software can run on different machines.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And, of course, provide Freddo with some company.

sentences.text: Farmer Juan Ángel Izquierdo says it is hard not to worry about wildfires In a small green meadow in the Gredos mountains, west of Madrid, a couple of dozen cows belonging to Juan Ángel Izquierdo and his family are grazing.

sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: St Paul's Pantry in Norton Lees has had to expand into the church building to accommodate all the people that use the food bank Volunteers at a community pantry say they fear they may have to close unless they can bring in additional donations of money and food.
sentences.article_title: Drop in donations puts community pantry at risk

sentences.text: Tina Sampson-Smith from St Paul's community pantry, in Norton Lees, Sheffield, said a drop off in donations and a rise in demand had left them in a precarious situation.
sentences.article_title: Drop in donations puts community pantry at risk

sentences.text: Asked how the coming weeks and months looked she replied: "They look pretty grim at the moment." According to the Trussell Trust more than 2.2m food parcels were given out in England in 2025, a 56% rise on 2019.
sentences.article_title: Drop in donations puts community pantry at risk

sentences.article_title: Drop in donations puts community pantry at risk

sentences.text: "Food poverty is really, really high at the moment and it's a never-ending battle to get food because our supermarkets haven't got the stock to give us," she said.
sentences.article_title: Drop in donations puts community pantry at risk

sentences.text: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die The empty building that used to be the home of Marks & Spencer in Aberdeen is one of the first things you see when you arrive off the train and come into the city centre.

sentences.text: As a teenager, I spent hours on Union Street, its main thoroughfare, nicknamed the Granite Mile after the local silver-grey stone.
sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: "I come to Union Street to take a bus somewhere else... there's nothing to shop for now… it's horrendous," complains Marie Sim, a lifelong Aberdeen resident.
sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: It's a similar story across the country: High Streets, once bursting with shops, hit first by the rise of out-of-town retail centres and then by online commerce.

sentences.text: But Aberdeen is in the thick of an ambitious turnaround plan.

sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: The Marks & Spencer flagship store in Aberdeen closed in August, 80 years after it opened there On top of that, the council is pouring tens of millions into trying to make the city centre a destination again.

sentences.text: Like many other places, it's leaning into the "experience economy", with a new indoor food and drink market and a major redevelopment of the seafront.

sentences.text: Politicians of all stripes have been trying for years to breathe new life into town centres - and Andy Burnham, who has made a focus on "place" part of his political identity, is the latest.
sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: One of the biggest obstacles is fractured ownership.
sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: Shops and buildings are often owned by dozens of different landlords, sometimes through offshore companies or complex structures, each with their own interests and priorities.
sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: That can slow decision-making and make large-scale regeneration difficult.
sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: In Aberdeen's boom years of North Sea oil, from the late 1970s through to the early 2010s, it didn't have to work hard to fill its hotels and restaurants and get the cash tills ringing because of the wealth the energy industry brought to the city.

sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: The prime minister told party activists in Liverpool that the new publicly owned company, branded Great British Grid, will speed up connections to the grid by driving up competition for connection projects.
sentences.article_title: Burnham says public body will invest in electricity grid

sentences.text: Burnham is putting the proposals at the heart of a new goal to bring UK energy costs in line with other nations in Europe within 10 years.
sentences.article_title: Burnham says public body will invest in electricity grid

sentences.text: He promised on Tuesday to have an "honest conversation" with the public and take on the "difficult issues" that have been ignored for too long.
sentences.article_title: Burnham says public body will invest in electricity grid

sentences.text: Burnham put greater public control of utilities at the centre of his pitch for power over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Burnham says public body will invest in electricity grid

sentences.text: "A publicly-owned company that will challenge the private sector operators," he told the Labour conference.
sentences.article_title: Burnham says public body will invest in electricity grid

sentences.text: "It will increase competition, drive down costs and speed up connections.
sentences.article_title: Burnham says public body will invest in electricity grid

sentences.text: "So businesses can expand and grow more quickly." There are a number of reasons for the high energy prices in the UK , part of which comes from state subsidies given to private companies to modernise the grid.
sentences.article_title: Burnham says public body will invest in electricity grid

sentences.article_title: Burnham says public body will invest in electricity grid

sentences.article_title: Burnham says public body will invest in electricity grid

sentences.text: Andy Burnham has promised that Labour will fight the next general election on a pledge to change the UK's voting system.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: In his first party conference speech as prime minister, he announced plans for a national commission to explore options for electoral reform.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: He invited other parties to work with the commission to ensure "everyone's vote counts, and everyone's voice is heard".
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: He has previously supported moves towards a proportional representation (PR) model, telling last year's conference that "PR's time has come".
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Westminster's first-past-the-post system, under which candidates with the most votes in each seat are elected, has been called into question as the UK political landscape has fragmented in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Debate over the system has intensified since Labour amassed a huge parliamentary majority with a 34% vote share in 2024.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Around 100 Labour MPs recently supported a parliamentary amendment in favour of setting up a commission to examine alternative options, a move Burnham himself supported last year when mayor of Greater Manchester.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Any move to change the voting system would be supported by the Liberal Democrats, who had previously urged Burnham to introduce proportional representation before the next election, which must be held by 2029.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: However, any move away from first-past-the-post is likely to be resisted by the Conservatives.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Reform UK backed introducing PR at the last election, but there has been speculation that its enthusiasm for the move may have since cooled.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Speaking to broadcasters after Burnham's speech, Reform leader Nigel Farage said he was open to debating a potential change to the system "at some point" but other issues were "far more urgent".
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: He added: "Is this an absolute priority for the general election after the next one?
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: I don't believe that it is." Support for changing the voting system is also not universal within Labour, with deputy leader Lucy Powell acknowledging that "parts of the Labour Party" are not in favour of it.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Speaking to Politics Live on BBC 2, she said she personally backed electoral reform but declined to specify a proposed new system, adding there were "lots of models" available.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: At the last UK election the Liberal Democrats backed the introduction of a single transferable vote (STV) system, which is used for Scottish council elections.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Other options include the additional member system, a hybrid model that combines first-past-the-post with regional party lists that is used to elect members of the Scottish Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Earlier this year, the Welsh Senedd was elected for the first time using a closed-list proportional representation system .
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: The Green Party supports electoral reform but Green MP Ellie Chowns said: "The PM cannot acknowledge the unfairness of a system capable of handing power to a government with a minority of the vote share, and then say the answer is to let that happen exactly once more before he fixes it.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: "Burnham must act with urgency to immediately jumpstart the National Commission, guarantee timely progress, and ensure its recommendations are delivered in time for a fairer voting system to be in place at the next general election." sentences.text: Angela Rayner took aim at the 'injustice' of leasehold in her conference speech Leaseholders will be given extra protections from "cowboy" property agents and hidden fees, Angela Rayner has announced.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The housing secretary told Labour's annual conference the government would legislate for a new independent regulator and launch a consultation to cap "rip off" administrative fees.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The changes would cover the estimated five million leaseholders in England and Wales who can be forced to pay a landlord for simple changes to their home, despite having bought it.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner told party activists she had heard of leaseholders being charged £250 for permission to own a pet and £400 to change their front door.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: She said people in these situations were "powerless against the vested interests that only take, while giving nothing back in return".
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The government is already legislating , external to ban new leasehold flats, described in Labour's 2024 election manifesto as a "feudal" system where people own the right to occupy a property via a lease for a limited number of years from a freeholder, or landlord, who owns the land.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Through the Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill , ministers want a commonhold system where residents collectively own and manage their buildings.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Now, Rayner is taking aim at the web of management companies that operate between leaseholders and their effective landlords.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: She said the sector had many decent businesses which were "undermined by far too many cowboys, crooks and con artists".
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: People excited at buying their own homes are "tricked" into using in-house services, meaning that "with no transparency or accountability, vultures can take advantage", Rayner added.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: "We will legislate for an independent regulation to rein these cowboys in," she said, announcing legislation for an independent watchdog of property agents.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: This includes estate agents, managing agents and estate managers.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: This regulator would be able to set codes of practice, such as standards of conduct and proper complaint handling for those they regulate, and property agents will be required to obtain a licence.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: If they fall foul of the required standards, the regulator would have the power to take their licenses away, the government added.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The government said it wanted to bring forward the changes "as soon as possible".
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner also said new legislation would create the power for caps on permission and administration fees leaseholders pay to landlords.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: These caps would cover freehold estates and privately managed estates where people can face additional fees for making cosmetic changes to their properties and requesting documents like building safety certificates.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: A public consultation will be launched to help decide the rate of caps.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: It comes in addition to an already-announced £250 cap on yearly ground rents paid by leaseholders in England and Wales, which had stalled during the change of prime minister over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The government has said it expects the limit on ground rents - an annual fee paid by leaseholders to their freeholder - to come into force in late 2028, but MPs have called for this to be brought forward to late 2027.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner said she was "capping and then scrapping" ground rents, indicating she may try to go further than a cap.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: In her speech, Rayner did not mention the government's housing target of building 1.5m homes in England by the next election.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: She admitted earlier this month there was only a "slim chance" of hitting it .
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Last week, ministers announced a new Your First Home policy to help first-time homebuyers in England with a deposit of 2.5%, similar to the Help To Buy scheme introduced under the Conservatives in 2013.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner also said she plans to strengthen council powers to take over empty homes to meet the need for council houses and tackle homelessness.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: But this was criticised by the Tories as a "desperate" attempt by Labour to try to hit its housing target.

sentences.text: John Healey and cabinet ministers from the other great offices of state gave speeches at Labour Party conference on Monday The chancellor has warned against allowing Britain's benefits bill to balloon while not offering young people opportunities.

sentences.text: John Healey told Labour's annual conference in Liverpool that cutting welfare spending was "more than an economic must - it's a moral duty".
sentences.article_title: Best thing we can offer young people is a job, not benefits, says chancellor

sentences.text: "The best thing we can offer a young person is not a benefit payment - it's a first job with training and a wage," he said.
sentences.article_title: Best thing we can offer young people is a job, not benefits, says chancellor

sentences.article_title: Best thing we can offer young people is a job, not benefits, says chancellor

sentences.article_title: Best thing we can offer young people is a job, not benefits, says chancellor

sentences.article_title: Best thing we can offer young people is a job, not benefits, says chancellor

sentences.article_title: Best thing we can offer young people is a job, not benefits, says chancellor

sentences.text: Through the scheme, which the Treasury says will roll out across England from March 2027, local teams plan to match young people with employers, including small businesses that have never taken on a trainee.

sentences.text: The department said an extra £100m was going into the scheme, "fully funded" by savings from the Department for Work and Pensions' crackdown on fraud.

sentences.text: Kanishka Narayan was appointed AI minister by Andy Burnham in July The government must "take seriously the possibility of an unprecedented impact on the jobs market" caused by artificial intelligence (AI), a UK minister has said.

sentences.text: Andy Burnham might be a new face at No 10, after ousting Sir Keir Starmer in July,  but his rise to power has been decades in the making.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: The 56-year-old started out as a special adviser and then an MP in Tony Blair's New Labour government.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: He first stood to be Labour leader back in 2010 and then again in 2015, when he came a distant second to Jeremy Corbyn, before turning his back on Westminster and re-inventing himself as the King of the North.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: As the first Mayor of Greater Manchester, he built a powerful political brand - affable, down-to-earth and, above all, proudly Northern.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: When asked by the website Mumsnet to name his favourite biscuit, the new prime minister replied that he did not have a sweet tooth and preferred "beer and chips and gravy".
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: From Manchester mayor to prime minister; what is his record and what does he stand for?
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Born in Liverpool in 1970, Burnham grew up in Culcheth, a quiet commuter belt village in Cheshire, near Warrington.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: His father, a BT engineer, and his mother, a GP receptionist, were both staunch Labour supporters and he developed an early interest in politics.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Burnham has described how he was inspired to join the Labour Party at the age of 14, after being moved by the BBC TV drama, Boys from the Blackstuff, about life on the dole in Liverpool.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: A lifelong Everton fan, his friends remember Burnham as a competitive, sports-mad child, who was a fast bowler for Lancashire schoolboys cricket team.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: At school, the local Roman Catholic comprehensive, his English teacher recalls how he stood to be a Labour candidate in mock elections - and won by a landslide.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Burnham credits his working-class Catholic upbringing for having a big impact on his politics, particularly teachings around social justice.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: He has described himself as "Catholic by upbringing" although "not particularly religious", but he was sworn in to Parliament over a Bible and will be the UK's first prime minister to enter Downing Street as a Catholic.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: While Burnham told the Times his mother would be "wearing her rosary beads out" to mark him becoming prime minister, his father, Roy, will unfortunately be unaware of his son's achievement due to his dementia.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: He told The Times:  "That's a sadness because he would be (proud).
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: The way I look at it, it's his achievement as well.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: "A whole family achievement although he doesn't know it." Burnham and his two brothers were the first in their family to go to university, with Andy studying English at Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: In his book, Head North, Burnham wrote that he "struggled to feel part of things" at university and felt like an "imposter".
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: However, the music-lover - who is a fan of Manchester indie bands like The Smiths and The Stone Roses - said his "growing interest in Manchester music gave me an identity and an advantage".
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Burnham appeared alongside Sir Keir Starmer during a visit by the PM to Ashton-under-Lyne in April After graduating, he started out in journalism, working for trade magazines including Tank World and Passenger World Management.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: In his early 20s, he got his first break in politics, working as a researcher for the late Tessa Jowell, then MP for Dulwich and West Norwood, who would go on to be a minister under Tony Blair and Gordon Brown.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Burnham rose quickly through the ranks, becoming a special adviser to Culture Secretary Chris Smith before being elected as the MP for his hometown of Leigh, in Greater Manchester, in 2001.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: He first served as a junior minister under Blair, but joined the cabinet as chief secretary to the Treasury, and later culture secretary and health secretary, under Brown.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: It was as secretary of state for culture, media and sport that Burnham was heckled at a memorial service marking the 20th anniversary of the Hillsborough disaster.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Ninety-seven Liverpool fans were killed in the stadium crush of 1989.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: The heckling spurred Burnham on to raise the issue in cabinet, contributing to the launch of a second inquiry into the disaster.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: A keen footballer, Burnham was a regular feature in the annual Labour MPs vs political journalists match In 2010, after Brown resigned following Labour's general election defeat, Burnham  ran to become the party's leader.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: He came fourth out of the five contenders, losing to Ed Miliband, but spent the next five years building up his appeal with the party's grassroots.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: In 2015 he tried again, beaten this time by Jeremy Corbyn.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Burnham's critics have branded him a weather vane, whose views have blown with the political winds to give him the best chance of success.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: He served in Corbyn's shadow cabinet, as shadow home secretary, despite being seen as on the Blairite centre-right of the party.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Burnham's views have moved increasingly to the left, backing the nationalisation of water and energy.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: He was not one of those who resigned in protest at Corbyn's leadership in 2016.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Instead he stood down in 2017 to run to be the first mayor of Greater Manchester.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Burnham won the contest with more than 60% of the vote and was re-elected by an even bigger margin in 2021.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Burnham gave a speech in 2014 at Anfield Stadium to mark the 25th anniversary of the Hillsborough disaster As mayor, he has drawn praise for his transformation of the region's transport system.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Under his leadership, Greater Manchester was the first area in England outside London to bring bus services back under public control, while integrating them with other modes of transport under the branding of the "Bee Network".
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Other bold pledges included ending rough sleeping in the region by 2020 - although the target was missed.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: His profile rose further during the Covid pandemic, when he accused the Conservative government of treating the north of England with "contempt" over regional lockdown restrictions.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: The stand-off helped earn him the nickname "King of the North".
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Burnham has hailed the "Bee Network" as one of his successes as mayor By the autumn party conference season of 2025, Burnham was openly on manoeuvres for the top job, as he refused to rule out a leadership bid.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: In January a potential opportunity for a return to Westminster arose when Greater Manchester MP Andrew Gwynne announced he was standing down, triggering a by-election in his Gorton and Denton constituency.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: However, Burnham was blocked from standing by Labour's ruling body, with the approval of the prime minister.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: By May, the situation had changed.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Labour suffered a poor set of election results in England, Scotland and Wales, with Reform riding high in the polls and the party seeing success in Burnham's backyard.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Sir Keir Starmer faced increased pressure over his future, with some MPs calling for change and ministerial resignations taking place.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Josh Simons announced he would step down as Labour MP for Makerfield to make way for Burnham to mount a bid to return to Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Burnham went on to be selected as the Labour candidate for the constituency and the following month he secured his return to Westminster.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: He was then elected unopposed to be leader of the Labour Party and prime minister within weeks.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: It might have felt like a seamless transition - but it was a huge political gamble that was not guaranteed to work.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: If he had failed to win the Makerfield by-election his political career would have effectively been over - and if all of his potential challengers for the Labour crown had not melted away, he might have ended up as a backbench MP.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Burnham made a confident start as PM, with a blizzard of eyecatching policies aimed at easing cost of living pressures and shifting power out of Westminster.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: One of his first acts was to set up No 10 North, in Manchester.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: Labour had a modest bounce in the opinion polls, edging in front of Reform UK for the first time in months.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: This prompted speculation that he might call an early election, which were quicky squashed by the new PM.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: But his hands remain tied by the manifesto Labour was elected on in 2024, with little room for manoeuvre on tax and spending.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power

sentences.text: And although he arrived for Labour's conference in Liverpool in a commanding position in the party, most of the really tough decisions he must take as prime minister  - from welfare reform to defence spending - lie ahead of him.

sentences.text: Mark and Roberta Harrison say Hobie was funny and mischievous The police watchdog has criticised a force after call handlers told a family raising mental health concerns to ring a locksmith.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: On 6 August 2025, Hobie Harrison's parents called Norfolk Police to request a welfare check after he failed to respond to them.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: He was found dead the next day.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said the force's 101 call handlers should have referred the family to mental health services, but instead suggested they contacted a locksmith.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Norfolk Police said it was reviewing the findings and it had been following the force's Right Care, Right Person (RCRP) policy , external , which limits officer attendance at welfare calls to cases involving "immediate risk to life".
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The IOPC said the call handlers should have asked more probing questions to assess Hobie's level of risk and there should have been a better explanation to his parents about why officers were not sent under its RCRP guidelines.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Hobie's parents, Mark and Roberta Harrison, made a second request for a welfare check for their son to Norfolk Police the following day.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Officers attended and found the 30-year-old dead in his flat in Norwich.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The couple say they were left unsure where to turn after being told their concerns for their son did not meet the threshold for a police response In October 2025, the family made a complaint to Norfolk Police over its handling of their call.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: In its report, the IOPC criticised Norfolk Police's response to that complaint after the force told the parents officers should not have attended either call, including the second one that led to Hobie's body being found.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The IOPC called that reply "unnecessary and insensitive".
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Hobie had previously threatened suicide and Mark said: "We'll never know whether he was still alive when we first called and whether something could have been done.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: David Ford, the watchdog's director of oversight and casework, said: "We have raised our concerns with the force around its interpretation of RCRP and monitoring of the initiative.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: "As a result... the force has said it will undertake a review to examine whether there are any organisational learnings." Norfolk Police said it could not comment further because an inquest has yet to take place, which is due to happen in November.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Hobie's parents say the 30-year-old loved music and enjoyed gardening Hobie had schizophrenia and developmental trauma and was under the care of the Norfolk and Suffolk Foundation Trust Community Mental Health Team.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: His parents said he had a history of drug use.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The couple adopted Hobie as a child and said he had been in "good spirits" the last time they saw him before his death.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: In August 2025, the family said they became concerned he had not spoken to them for more than 24 hours as he usually contacted them "several times a day".
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: "The non-contact was just... it didn't happen.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: So, it was very, very unusual," said Roberta.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The couple went to Hobie's flat but could not use their key to get inside because his key was still in the lock on the inside of the door.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: "We were 100% certain he was in there and he wasn't responding, so we knew there was something seriously wrong," said Mark.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: If you have been affected by any of the issues in this story, you can visit the BBC Action Line for support and information Unable to break in, they called Norfolk Police and told call handlers that their son had a history of self-harm and suicidal threats.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: After consulting a supervisor, the staff member told them the situation did not meet the threshold for a police response and suggested they consider contacting a locksmith.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: "We didn't know how to make a decision at that point or what to do quite frankly," said Roberta.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The following morning, after a second call to police, officers attended the flat and found Hobie's body.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: "If the police are no longer going to come, then it has to be very clear who's got the responsibility," Roberta added.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The Harrisons say regular calls, walks, shopping trips and meals together formed part of their daily routine with Hobie RCRP was first developed by Humberside Police in 2019 and has since been adopted by forces across England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The policy is intended to reduce police involvement in welfare and mental health-related incidents so officers can focus on crime and immediate threats to life.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Norfolk Police said the approach, which it introduced in 2024, had reduced officer attendance at welfare-related incidents, from 11,831 in the year before the policy was introduced to 9,229 by its second year.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The force said there was "no defined response" to welfare concerns and the appropriate pathway depended on the circumstances.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: His family say Hobie enjoyed riding his bike when he felt well enough to get out and about The Norfolk and Suffolk Integrated Care Board said support could involve health, social care, ambulance or police services.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: A 2024 national agreement on the policy , external said people experiencing mental health crises should not be left without support.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Some coroners have raised concerns about RCRP.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: A Prevention of Future Deaths  report into the death of Sophie Cotton in County Durham , external said the policy appeared to overlook that mental health teams could not enter locked premises.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Reports into the deaths of Paul Alexander in West Yorkshire , external and Andrew Hughes in Manchester , external also highlighted gaps in RCRP response arrangements.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Mindy says people often presume she is straight because of her age As a 75-year-old lesbian, Mindy Meleyal has lived through every major milestone in the modern LGBT rights movement, from the start of decriminalisation in 1967 to the first same-sex marriages in 2014.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: But now she says this important part of her identity is frequently overlooked due to her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: She's part of England's older LGBTQ+ community, which a new report suggests often experiences poorer health, more limited finances and greater social isolation than the wider older population.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report, from the Centre for Ageing Better, says without specialist support, this growing demographic could be forced "back into the closet" when accessing care, warning they may even delay getting the care they need because of concerns about homophobia.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Adam Preston, a housing development manager from the LGBT Foundation charity, says he regularly meets older members of the community in exactly that situation.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It's very common for people to hide things if they have a carer visiting their home, for example hiding their wedding photos or taking down a trans flag," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston is part of the team behind Kindred House, a first-of-its-kind LGBTQ+ social housing scheme for over-55s, set to open in Manchester next year.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: An artist's impression of what Kindred House will look like when it opens The scheme, a joint project with the local council, will provide 80 self-contained apartments and communal areas available to the local community.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The majority of residents will be LGBTQ+.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The Kindred House scheme is what's known as extra-care housing, which means residents live independently, but there is a 24/7 care team available for those who need extra help, and all staff will receive specialist training around LGBTQ+ inclusion.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston says he hopes the scheme will "trigger some conversations" about how to best support older LGBTQ+ people in the challenges they face.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Mindy and her wife Linda have been together for more than 30 years, but says they're often mistaken for sisters.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "She's 18 inches taller than me, I've got a Yorkshire accent and she's got a Northern Irish accent," Mindy says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I think it's pretty obvious we weren't brought up in the same building." She believes part of that is often down to people presuming she is straight because of her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "There are different tribes of people in every age group, but when you get older, people start clumping you together with other stereotypes," she says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: After divorcing her husband and coming out as lesbian, Mindy co-founded a lesbian commune in Hull before moving to Manchester On one occasion, while Mindy was in hospital after a stroke, a nurse referred to Linda as Mindy's husband.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: She said it was not only "insulting", but made her consider what sort of training the staff might have had.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The Spotlight on Ageing report says these sort of experiences can also have an impact on the support people receive.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Sarah Wilkinson, research and analysis manager at the Centre for Ageing Better, says after a "lifetime of homophobia and transphobia", older LGBTQ+ people now face the "additional, and overlapping, challenge of ageism".
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report , external says older LGBTQ+ people are less likely to have children - someone born in 1950 would have been in their 50s by the time same-sex couples could legally adopt - and that they are more likely to be estranged from their families when compared to their heterosexual counterparts.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report also found more than half of gay and bisexual men aged 65 and above live alone, compared with less than a quarter of heterosexual men.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Bisexual women aged 50 to 64 are twice as likely as their heterosexual peers to live alone.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: It also suggests that only half of gay and bisexual men aged 50 and above definitely agree they would have someone to help them if they needed, 14 percentage points lower than heterosexual men of the same age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Norman Goodman, 75, came out as bisexual in his late 60s after the death of his wife Marilyn.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The couple never had children, and Norman now has no immediate family nearby to help him with things like hospital visits or housework.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: He says his support system comes in the form of his partner Tony, and a group of friends and neighbours he refers to as his "chosen family".
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I'm lucky, I've got great friends and great neighbours, and I know I can knock on somebody's door day or night and I could get help," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Norman came out as bisexual when he was in his 60s and says he relies on "chosen family" to support him But despite having their support while he's relatively independent, Norman says he worries about the prospect of facing discrimination if he needs more formal care as he ages.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "Hopefully I will maintain and look after myself the best I can, but I've heard horror stories of gay people in nursing homes being treated terribly," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I think nurses, doctors, carers should all be trained on how to look after LGBT people." It's the reason behind schemes like Manchester's Kindred House, which are not unusual in other parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: There are similar projects in Spain, Sweden, Germany, the US and Canada, but in the UK they are few and far between.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: In 2021, the UK's first LGBTQ+ retirement community, Tonic, opened in London with 19 apartments for affordable rental or shared ownership.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The scheme attracted so much attention, later this year it is set to feature in a Netflix documentary telling the story of one of its first residents, Chek Min-Ong.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: After 43 years together, Min, 77, and his late partner Tim, had discussed their plans for a future where one of them would live alone, as Tim's health deteriorated.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Min and his late partner Tim wanted to make sure they lived somewhere supportive when one of them passed away "Tim and I have always had this very open discussion, we wanted to know, when one of us is not here anymore, the other person will have a community and feel safe," Min says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: When Tim died five months after moving into Tonic, Min says his new-found community rallied around him.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It is what [Tim and I] always wanted, that we'd never have to explain ourselves," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "We'd never have to face a question and feel guilty about not telling the full story, or having to lie.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "You're just here, being yourself." While schemes like Kindred House and Tonic are welcomed by Mindy, Norman and Min, the Spotlight on Ageing report warns that, because the older LGBTQ+ population is growing, the demand for specialist services is expected to outstrip supply.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Between 2019 and 2024, the number of over-50s identifying as lesbian, gay or bisexual in the UK increased by around a third - from roughly 340,000 to almost 460,000.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: There was a 4% rise in the number of heterosexual people aged 50 and above in the same period.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: These numbers are projected to continue to increase as the relatively larger younger generations of people identifying as LGBTQ+ age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston warns that without more schemes like Kindred House, and more training and awareness for those in other care settings, the ageing population may struggle to get proper support.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: For Mindy, who is part of a steering group advising on the plans, knowing there may be more options available in the future is reassuring.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It's important that you can go, that you think, 'You know what, I could live there because I know the staffing, the ethics, the rules, everything about the place has been put together from an LGBTQ+ focus,'" she says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "That's what we've been doing and it's something I'm really proud of being a part of."
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Overcoming social anxiety can be tricky but experts have shared some tips to try and make it easier It was during her teenage years that Mary began to become anxious in social situations.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It got so bad she developed depression and had to have time off school.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: By the time she started university, she avoided group settings altogether.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I didn't join clubs and societies like others did," says Mary (not her real name).
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I just thought nobody would want to get to know me.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I didn't really make a single friend during my whole degree." Mary's social anxiety was so bad that she was diagnosed as having social anxiety disorder - something that affects up to 12% of people , external at some point in their lives.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: But plenty more report struggling more generally.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: As students return to uni, we asked experts how to overcome these feelings whether in your first, or final year.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: This video can not be played What makes you socially anxious?
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Research has suggested more than a fifth of university students face some kind of social anxiety during their studies – and it has been linked to lower grades, poorer relationships and isolation in a study by the University of Chichester , external .
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: For many, university marks the first time they have moved out of home – and the expectation is that they will quickly make friends.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Mary, who went to the University of Exeter, says she did try.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "When I first got there I went to one society, but everybody was talking to each other and I had a sudden fear come over me.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I felt I wouldn't fit in and I went home." Mary, who is now 25, describes her social anxiety as like an out of body experience.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: When she was talking to new people, heat would rise in her face and her hands would begin to tingle.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I'd almost feel myself separating from my body.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I forgot how to form words," she says.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "After social situations I was often left with the sense that I'd done something awful.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I had an all-consuming feel of shame.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I kept thinking there was something fundamentally flawed in me." Neil Greening, chair of the Social Anxiety Alliance UK, says this is a typical characteristic of people with social anxiety.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "People think they have a personality flaw.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: They internalise it rather than seeing it as a recognisable condition that they can get help for." The key thing to remember: It's fairly normal to feel a little shy or anxious when meeting new people, being in new situations or going for a job interview.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Social anxiety is when it actually stops people doing things, Greening says.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: For those with a clinical diagnosis it can have a debilitating impact like it did for Mary.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "It can be hard to admit to any form of social anxiety in a world where extrovertism and social confidence is generally admired.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Mary, who has moved on to do a postgraduate course, is now managing her social anxiety better.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: After her undergraduate degree she got support from the NHS in the form of a talking therapy called CBT.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It is considered the gold standard treatment for social anxiety and encourages people to re-frame their thoughts and change their behaviours.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Prof David Clark, a psychologist at the University of Oxford, says he would like to see more people come forward for therapy but says people can also take steps to help themselves.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: The first step, he says, is to stop obsessive self-focus .
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "People with social anxiety often monitor themselves constantly during social situations.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "Focus outwardly on the conversation, other person or your surroundings." He says you also need to test your fears with behavioural experiments by asking a question in a meeting or saying something in a group and noticing what happens.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "People with social anxiety often assume negative outcomes – that they will embarrass themselves or think others will find them boring.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Testing that can help people break that.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It's frightening, but it can really help." He also says they need to drop safety behaviours , such as rehearsing every sentence, avoiding eye contact or sticking close to one particular person.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: And finally, Clark adds, try to avoid post-event rumination .
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "It's so easy to distort what actually happened." This is something Mary can empathise with.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I used to play things over constantly in my mind.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: What I've learnt is that dealing with social anxiety is a gradual process.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: The therapy really helped me, but so did something a friend said to me a couple of years ago.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "When I said I didn't want to join her in meeting some of her friends, citing my poor social skills, she said she'd never thought that about me and that I shouldn't undersell myself.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I was overcome with emotion.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I'm now pushing myself to engage more.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It helps that in my postgrad course we're in smaller groups, but I've also joined an astronomy group.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Have you ever slept next to a snoring partner and woken up feeling stressed, unfocused or forgetful the next day?
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: As snoring is relatively common, it is often left untreated and dismissed as a harmless irritation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But according to experts, sleeping next to a snorer could be impacting your health.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Snoring is caused by the vibration of the soft tissues in our upper airways during sleep, explains Dr Clare Simon, a dentist with a special interest in dental sleep medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: About 40% of the UK adult population snores, with the issue affecting more men than women, says the British Snoring and Sleep Apnoea Association (BSSAA).
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: And 75% of people with a snoring partner say they have had their sleep impacted, according to a US survey by the Sleep Foundation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Sarah Mackay, known as @fitwsarah online, says her energy levels change through her cycle A woman points to a colour-coded grid dividing the menstrual cycle into four phases, each paired with a different list of exercises.

sentences.text: This is one of thousands of videos on TikTok and Instagram suggesting that people change their workouts depending on where they are in their menstrual cycles - something known as 'cycle-syncing'.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: So-called cycle-syncing workout plans have surged in popularity online, with Google searches for the term rising 740% since 2022 and more than 55,000 TikTok videos now using the #cyclesyncing hashtag.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Most of the advice is shared by fitness and wellness creators rather than medical or research experts.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Kelly McNulty, a researcher at Leeds Beckett University specialising in menstrual cycles and exercise, says there is evidence that some women experience changes in symptoms, energy or perceived strength across their cycle.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But that is different from evidence that all women should train in a particular way at a particular point, she tells the BBC, adding that these videos are "a trend based on marketing rather than any kind of research or evidence".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "There isn't any research to support that kind of phase-based prescription," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts
