sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: A key issue is that menstrual cycles are highly individual, McNulty adds - they can differ between women, and one woman's experience can also change from one cycle to the next.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: That makes the blanket advice often found on social media difficult to apply, she explains.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Many cycle-tracking apps and programmes are also designed around relatively regular menstrual cycles that are 21 to 35 days, which can make their recommendations less applicable to people with irregular periods, or those using hormonal contraception.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She doesn't follow a prescriptive plan, she says, but instead makes changes intuitively.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my luteal phase I'll try and ease off in the training," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my follicular phase, I'm so energised, I feel like I can lift so much heavier.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: I like to try and get my long runs in." Burgoyne also welcomes the growing attention on women's health, and says that exercise and nutrition research has historically focused heavily on male bodies, with findings then often applied to women.

sentences.text: Sarah says she has sometimes hit personal records while on her period Fitness creator Sarah Mackay, known as @liftwsarah on Instagram and TikTok, has also noticed her energy, motivation, cramps and mood change through the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But she deliberately avoids strict plans because, she says, "there are too many variables at play".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Some online plans advise women to avoid intense training during their period, she says, yet she has sometimes hit personal records while menstruating.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "The problem is not that the menstrual cycle is irrelevant," she says, but that "not everything is predictable".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Dr Faye Bate, a trained medical doctor and women's health expert, is also wary of advice suggesting all women should train differently according to their menstrual phase.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "A one-size-fits-all model of 'you should be exercising this way in this phase and a different way in a different phase' shouldn't be advice that applies to all women," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She is concerned that repeatedly telling women they are likely to be weaker or less capable at particular points in their cycle could create a "nocebo" effect - where negative expectations themselves influence how someone feels or performs.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty tells the BBC that routinely easing off resistance training could also limit progress.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Strength training is particularly important for women, who face a higher risk of osteoporosis later in life.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: While cycle-syncing itself may not be backed by strong evidence, the experts we spoke to did suggest being "cycle-aware".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty says tracking your cycle can be a useful way to understand your own patterns, while Dr Bate also encourages women to become more familiar with how they feel at different points in the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Both welcome the fact that menstrual health is being discussed more openly, but say the focus should be on individual experience, rather than rigid, phase-based rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In practice, that might mean having painkillers ready before your period, taking a rest day when symptoms are worse, or easing off a workout if you feel unusually fatigued.

sentences.text: For Dr Bate, "the most important part is tuning in to how you feel".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has signalled she is willing to rethink plans to make it harder for foreign workers to claim permanent residence in the UK.

sentences.text: Dr Chris McCarthy says the pillow that's best for you depends on the way you sleep (branding has been obscured) "I am one of those people," says Dr Chris McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "I do take my pillow with me." You may have seen those people at the airport - a pillow stuffed under an arm as they drag their suitcases to check-in.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Or you might be one yourself - attached to a pillow that's soft enough to settle into but robust enough that it's not bunched into a ball by morning.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy insists he's not being fussy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He's a top physiotherapist and knows the wrong pillow can be a pain in the neck.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He doesn't take his abroad, but as soon as he gets to his hotel he starts "faffing about" with the pillows - and he's got a tried and tested trick to make even the most lacklustre one fit for sleep.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Here's his guide to choosing the perfect pillow for you.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: What makes the perfect pillow?
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: One advertised for your sleeping position?
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Sliced Bread separates science fact from the marketing fiction.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy, an associate professor at the Manchester School of Physiotherapy, says the right pillow will depend on what position you sleep in.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He tells the BBC's Sliced Bread podcast that most people fall into one of three categories of sleeper: side, back or front.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy discourages front sleeping as your neck is turned one way for a long period of time.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "Inevitably a muscle or ligament gets stretched and a bit irritated," he says.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "If there's one thing there's a really good consensus on... in the physiotherapy world about treating spinal pain, it's don't sleep on your front." When choosing a pillow, back sleepers should consider the flexion at the top of their spine, a curving that increases naturally in many people as they age.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: If you have a bigger bend "it means you need a slightly thicker pillow than someone who's got a very flat back," says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: For side sleepers the key measurement is the width of your shoulders.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: In general, the broader you are the thicker the pillow you will need.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: But you also need to consider your mattress.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy says how much you sink into your mattress "makes a huge difference in the subsequent height you then need from the pillow".
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "Broad shoulders need a thick pillow [if] you're on a very firm mattress," he explains.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "If you're on a softer mattress, then you need a thinner pillow because your shoulder sinks into the mattress [more]." This is less of an issue for back sleepers as they don't sink into the mattress as much as side sleepers do.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: If your pillow feels too flat, McCarthy suggests placing a folded towel underneath and changing the number of folds to adjust the height.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Then you can make a rough measurement to help you pick a new one.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Specialist pillows are often advertised as contoured, ergonomic or orthopaedic - but McCarthy says their effectiveness isn't completely proven.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "There is a little bit of fairly scrappy evidence to suggest that having a little bit of a higher front of the pillow, which goes into the neck area... does help [side sleepers]." To see if a higher front helps you sleep better, you can try McCarthy's towel trick by rolling it and placing it underneath your pillow.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He urges side sleepers to pick a position that keeps their back straight.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: For back sleepers, some manufacturers advertise a pillow with a dip in the middle that is raised at the sides.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: It does put people into a good sleeping position, says McCarthy, but some of his patients have found them "a bit claustrophobic".
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Someone who has a large and heavy head also needs a thicker and firmer pillow, he adds.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Feather and down can keep you cool on warm nights because they wick away heat from your head, says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: But they can change shape during the night, particularly if the sleeper moves around a lot and the pillow can end up bunched towards the headboard.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "What starts off as a nice, flat, supported surface becomes a wedge and so your neck is then kinked up." Hollow fibre and microfibre fillings can hold shape better though they generally don't wick away heat as well, says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Some are made with a firmer material in the lower half of the pillow, which help retain the shape during the night.

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In a blog post, WhatsApp, clarified parents would not be given the power to see the messages their teen is sending and receiving, which along with calls would stay private and protected by end-to-end encryption.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And they will have the option of choosing between the default 13+ setting for Meta AI, the app's optional built-in AI assistant, or a stricter "Limited Content" option.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "All of these controls are being designed to support open conversations about how to use WhatsApp between parents and teens, while keeping everyone's personal messages private," the company said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The changes come as pressure mounts on tech companies from governments and regulators to change the way they operate in order to better protect children using their platforms.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In June, the government announced it plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms, with the restrictions expected to come into force in March 2027.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It said "highly effective age assurance" measures would be used to check the age of those using social media.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: WhatsApp is currently excluded from the ban because the government considers it a messaging service.

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: England's biggest school leaders' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections, saying they could pose a "risk to life" for school staff.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) said the change to inspections, rolled out nationally just under a year ago, had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: It said schools should instead be rated using short narrative reports that set out their strengths and areas they could improve.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted said it had worked closely with unions and parents to develop the new report card inspection system and that it would continue to grade schools.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted, England's schools inspectorate, introduced the report card system to replace its previous one or two-word judgements last November, following the death of head teacher Ruth Perry , who took her own life after Ofsted downgraded her school from "outstanding" to "inadequate".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An inquest ruled that an Ofsted inspection had contributed to her death in January 2023.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: That led to a change in how Ofsted assessed schools, bringing in report cards designed to grade schools on several areas, rather than focusing on one overall grade.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An example of a new Ofsted inspection report But the new system has faced criticism since it was first proposed , with Perry's sister Prof Julia Waters saying it appeared to be "a rehash of the discredited and dangerous system it is meant to replace".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The NAHT issued a claim in the High Court for a judicial review over the changes, arguing there had not been adequate consultation on the new report cards before they were introduced, but this was rejected.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Nearly a year after it was fully rolled out, the NAHT said evidence from its members suggested the new system is having a detrimental impact on school leaders' mental health.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Testimonies seen by the BBC suggest head teachers are being left "overwhelmed" and "anxious", with the pressure caused by the inspections described as "intolerable".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Although the system had been changed with the intention of lowering the burden on school leaders, the testimonies say the inspection and assessment process had become "higher stakes than ever before".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Amanda Hulme, head teacher at Claypool Primary School in Bolton, said a recent inspection at her school had been "easily the most stressful experience" of her career.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "It was definitely damaging to my health and really quite distressing," she said.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "I couldn't sleep and it led to my blood pressure and pulse rate increasing.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Powell told LBC earlier this month that she took head teacher wellbeing "incredibly seriously" and that the system of accountability needed to be "supportive and understanding.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "I'll continue the work that I do with head teachers, head teacher representatives and others to make sure that we get this Ofsted framework, but also the culture and the whole regime, right," she said.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The NAHT said the results of a recent survey of its members suggested that the majority who responded felt that inspections had worsened in the past 12 months.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The union is now calling for inspections to pause to allow for a "fundamental review of how inspection works", drawing on examples from other nations.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: In Wales, the inspectorate Estyn has removed judgements such as "excellent" and "good" from its reports, instead summarising findings by highlighting a school's strengths and areas for improvement.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Northern Ireland's Education and Training Inspectorate (ETI) also uses narrative reports without grades.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Scotland's His Majesty's Inspectorate of Education (HIME) does use grades, but there has been a recent consultation on their use.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: NAHT general secretary Paul Whiteman said: "The clear theme emerging across all the feedback we have received is that this Ofsted framework is even more stressful than the one that preceded it.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "Ofsted exists to raise standards for children and to provide clear reporting to parents," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "We will continue to engage closely with trades unions – but we will also continue to grade schools." Have you been impacted by the issues discussed in this story?

sentences.text: Schools are "crying out" for guidance from government on how pupils and teachers can use AI safely and effectively, a new report has warned.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: Sir Anthony Seldon, former head teacher and author on AI in education, says the technology is being used more and more frequently, but that its introduction has been "chaotic and anarchic".
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: His report calls for the government to roll out a national framework for adopting AI in education in England, including training teachers on how to use it, which schools should use to develop their own "AI strategies" by September next year.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: The government says its changes to the curriculum in England will give children digital skills and help them spot disinformation.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: Sir Anthony's report, co-authored with venture capitalist Tim Bunting, says schools have not been prepared for AI's arrival.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: Sir Anthony co-founded the group AI in Education, which was set up in 2023 to help educational institutions navigate AI safely.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: His report argues that getting a grip of AI requires the same level of national urgency as wars and epidemics, and requires a taskforce modelled on the one which helped to roll out the Covid vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: "Put simply, education has not kept pace with how – and how much – young people are already using AI, and that gap is starting to show up as a loss of perceived value in the institution itself," the report says.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the Department for Education says ministers take the "significant opportunities and challenges" of AI "incredibly seriously".
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: As well as refreshing the curriculum in England, they say they are building new AI tutoring tools and introducing new vocational routes to get children into successful careers.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: Some schools have already embedded AI into the curriculum.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: Benjamin Barker, principal at King's Leadership Academy Wavertree, says he wants his students to learn how to use tools safely, while also developing their critical thinking skills.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: Student Emma, 12, says she uses AI for her robotics projects, as well as proof-reading her English homework, and believes more students should be taught how to use it responsibly.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: "AI is coming into the future.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: It's getting more advanced," she says.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: "There's no way we're going to completely pull back from it.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: So I think that we should use it to be better people." How have you been affected by the issues raised in this story?

sentences.text: Lisa Carroll was only 41 was she was diagnosed with the rare form of ovarian cancer A mum-of-three who was diagnosed with a rare cancer has urged other women not to dismiss their symptoms.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: When Lisa Carroll, 47, from Coventry, returned from a family holiday in August 2021, she thought she was suffering from irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), a kidney infection or something minor.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Instead, she was told it was mucinous ovarian cancer (MOC), one of the rarest forms of ovarian cancer in the UK.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "I thought I had possibly a bit of IBS or a kidney problem or something like that.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: I was in quite a lot of pain," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Next year, Carroll and her husband are looking forward to celebrating their 20th wedding anniversary After calling NHS 111, Carroll was sent to hospital in Coventry where medics discovered a 12cm cyst on her right ovary.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: She was told it did not appear particularly sinister and was placed on a waiting list for surgery.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "Within a month, a cyst the size of a fist had grown to the point that I could feel it like a football in my stomach.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Pain and discomfort got worse and I felt shattered emotionally and physically", she said.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: By December, scans revealed the tumour had grown to 20cm and was beginning to rupture, so three days later she underwent an emergency procedure to remove the tumour, a fallopian tube, her appendix and surrounding tissue.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Two weeks later, doctors gave her the diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Following surgeries and chemotherapy, Carroll is approaching her five-year anniversary of being cancer free The cancer is exceptionally rare, with only around 200 cases diagnosed annually in the UK, said Ovacome, an ovarian cancer charity.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "Some ovarian cancers are really sneaky, hang around for years and you've got no sign of any symptoms at all", said Carroll, who works as the CEO of Lifespace Trust, a Warwickshire-based charity for young people.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "The fact that mine grew so quickly was what alerted them as early as they did." Yet despite losing her hair and enduring months of treatment, she says the biggest challenge was something she had not been prepared for.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "I got chucked into early menopause and that was the bit I massively struggled with.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: I didn't know what was depression and what was menopause." The Ovacome charity is hosting a fundraising walk in Cannon Hill Park, Birmingham on Saturday "I didn't know what was a cancer symptom and what was a menopause symptom.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: I couldn't open the washing machine, the dishwasher or the oven.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: I couldn't cook anything on the hob because I'd just have this awful hot flush.

sentences.text: University applicants in England will be given clearer information about student loans before they take them out, the government has said.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Ministers said they would spell out that governments can change repayment rules and that different career choices can affect how much borrowers repay.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: They agreed to some but not all of the recommendations made by MPs after an inquiry into student loans, and did not say whether they would reverse a freeze to the repayment threshold for some graduates.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The inquiry found the way loans had been presented to teenagers amounted to mis-selling , after the BBC revealed the Department for Education (DfE) had compared repayments to £30-a-month phone contracts.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The recent debate has centred around Plan 2 loans, which were issued in England between September 2012 and July 2023, and are still issued in Wales.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The interest rate on those loans is the Retail Prices Index (RPI) measure of inflation plus up to 3% depending on earnings, and borrowers repay at a rate of 9% of everything they earn over a repayment threshold, which is meant to rise with inflation every year.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The loans are written off after 30 years.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Campaigners want a lower interest rate, a lower repayment rate and for the government to reverse a decision last year to freeze the threshold at £29,385 for three years in England.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Freezing that threshold means graduates start repaying their loans sooner and, once they do, they pay more than they would have done if it had risen with inflation.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: MPs on the Treasury Committee called for a U-turn on that decision as part of a series of recommendations after an inquiry this summer.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: It also said "more can be done to help student loan borrowers understand how their loan balance may change over the long term".
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The government also said giving students long-term predictions of how much they might ultimately repay risked being "misleading" because of "limited" accuracy.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: It proposed instead to "demonstrate how different life and career choices may affect repayment trajectories", including salary progression, retraining, part-time work, and career breaks.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Nick Hillman, director of the Higher Education Policy Institute, who helped design the Plan 2 system, said the government had "absolutely rejected" most of what the Treasury Committee had recommended and its response would not meet the concerns of Plan 2 graduates.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: While Dame Meg Hillier, chair of the Treasury Committee, said making information clearer was "an important step" but "doesn't help graduates who are angry that they didn't receive the same service and are now facing punitive repayment terms on a loan which keeps growing".
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: She urged the chancellor to reverse the threshold freeze in this autumn's Budget.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (Pisa) saw reading and maths scores slump in each UK nation except England, while all four saw an uptick in science, with that rise again most notable in England.

sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.article_title: OpenAI scraps rollout of new model over safety concerns

sentences.text: The BBC spoke to parents and experts to find out their back-to-school tips It's back-to-school time again - and families brace for the challenge of swapping summer lie-ins for school routines, easing first-day nerves and getting ready for the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: While children in Scotland returned to school in mid-August, children in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be returning in the coming week as September begins.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: We spoke to experts to find out their six key tips to make going back to school as stress-free as possible.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Cerys Parker, a teacher and blogger, says one of the best ways to keep organised during school time is to keep a consistent morning routine.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Her morning starts 30 minutes before her children wake up, for some alone time and a hot coffee.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She  then makes them the same breakfast every morning, which they eat together with no screens, then it's upstairs for showers and getting ready for school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker also keeps copies of her children's timetables so she knows what to prepare on specific days, such as when they have PE She grabs their lunch boxes and they leave the house at 07:30 for the bus, or 07:50 if Parker is dropping them at school on the way to her own job.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The night before, she makes sure school bags are packed, shoes are ready, uniform is laid out and lunch is packed for the morning.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "We have things in the same place, so the bags are always in the same location, the keys, and that makes the morning smoother.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: There's no panic about where everything's going to be." It is easy to forget non-uniform days, sports days or study sessions.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker recommends having a family calendar pinned to your wall or your fridge - somewhere you can easily see it every day.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's an academic year calendar with a space for each of us, and then an events section, so as soon as a notice comes in, I write it down." This could include things like meal plans, after-school activities or - depending on your child's age - exams.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: After school, many children are tired and are not up for discussion about their day, so Will Shield, professor of child and educational psychology at the University of Exeter, suggests changing your approach to the conversation.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask some open questions, instead of interrogating them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask what made you smile today?
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Or who did you play with at lunchtime?" These sorts of questions are a lot easier to answer for a child, he says, instead of asking what they did.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "See it as part of the process of separating and loving you, missing you, which is really important." Many families will have children attending school for the first time, which can be just as big a moment for parents as it is for new pupils.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Shield says parents should "reassure themselves" about the routine they will need to follow on school mornings.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Visit the school, walk or drive past it, bring bedtimes back a bit earlier so it's not just a big start in the first week," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's about much more basic things, like feeling comfortable and safe to be in a classroom with other children," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Building independence can also help bridge the gap between home and school life, she says, by encouraging your child to do some things by themselves, such as zipping up their own coat.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's just building that sense of, I'm ready to do this without you," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: But Deiros Collado also stresses that your child should be able to ask for help when they need it.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "One of the best skills you can give your little ones is being able to say to an adult, 'Help me,' because you want your kid to be able to say that to a teacher." She also suggests a "goodbye ritual" with your child to practise separation, such as blowing a kiss.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Katharine Radice says that focusing too much on the homework outcome you want for your child can be "demotivating" for them Katharine Radice, teacher and author, recommends putting together a homework timetable.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Doing this puts boundaries around homework and makes it easier to ring-fence distraction-free time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: This could be different every week depending on different activities, but Radice stresses there should be a plan in advance so it's not left to the last minute.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: For supporting children with homework, Radice suggests approaching the task in a "positive and open way" and listening to what they might be finding difficult.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She also recommends looking for opportunities to praise your child's effort in doing work to help them "stay motivated." "If your child thinks their outcomes won't meet your expectations, they may start to feel that their effort is pointless," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Some children who are returning to school may have anxieties about the year ahead, and Shield recommends to sit with your child and listen to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Don't immediately reassure them by saying, 'You'll be fine,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "The child's got no evidence they will be fine because they're worried." He suggests phrases such as "I can see you're worried" to make a child feel listened to.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: It is also worth trying to dig deeper to find out what is making them worried about school specifically.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: He also recommends some gentle encouragement of positive things they like about school to ease some worries, such as lunchtime or playing sports with friends.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: If anxiety does become overwhelming for them, if they aren't sleeping or it is stopping them from doing everyday things, then Shield recommends talking to the school or a local GP.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Share your challenges, tips and questions with us ahead of the return to school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Dame Esther Rantzen, who has died at the age of 86, was best known for presenting the BBC TV programme That's Life!
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Over two decades, what started as a consumer programme with quirky asides became renowned for its high-profile campaigns, notably against child abuse.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: It resulted in Dame Esther setting up Childline, a national telephone helpline for children suffering abuse or neglect.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: She later became a renowned campaigner for older people and, in the last years of her life, for the legalisation of medically-assisted death.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Dame Esther Rantzen, broadcaster, campaigner and charity founder, dies aged 86 How That's Life! gave Esther Rantzen a career-defining moment Esther Louise Rantzen was born in Berkhamsted, Hertfordshire on 22 June 1940.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Her paternal ancestors were Polish Jews.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Her father, Henry, who worked as a broadcast engineer for the BBC, had moved the family out of London to escape German bombing during World War Two.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: The family returned to London when the war ended.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: She later recalled she hated the grey streets of the capital after the semi-rural idyll in which she had spent her early childhood.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: After a spell at a private school, run by what she recalled was a sadistic headmistress, she went to the North London Collegiate School in Edgware, and then to Somerville College, Oxford, where she read English.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Rantzen [centre] had an idyllic early childhood She became an enthusiastic member of the Oxford University Dramatic Society and of the Experimental Theatre Group.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Rantzen then secured a job as a trainee studio manager with BBC Radio, before moving to television as a researcher on the satirical show BBC3, which had been created by Ned Sherrin.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: She met documentary maker Desmond Wilcox when she approached him in a BBC bar and asked him to give a talk to a local youth club.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: He asked her to dinner and offered her a job on Man Alive, the BBC's current affairs programme.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: OpenAI has been at the centre of new concerns over uncontrolled AI activity OpenAI has acknowledged that it alerted "dozens" of global institutions that their websites may have been meddled with by its AI bots acting improperly.

sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: Nevertheless, OpenAI admitted: "This is not an appropriate use of this data." It added that the leak of user images occurred before it had put in place new safeguards on AI training, and it was working to get all the user images transferred to any third-party removed.

sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: Egyptian sculptures are among the collection at the British Museum in London Overseas visitors will not be charged to enter England's national museums after ministers decided against changing the universal free admission policy.

sentences.text: It comes after months of discussions between the government, museums, the tourism sector and local leaders to examine whether making tourists from abroad pay could boost the institutions' finances.

sentences.text: In March, the government said it would explore charging international visitors to enter national museums as it looks for ways to tackle funding pressures.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: But the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) has now said this could deter domestic visitors and that any benefits of charging would not be felt equally across the sector.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: The UK's 15 national museums, including 12 in London, have been free for all to enter since 2001.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: But a review published last year by former Labour minister Baroness Margaret Hodge suggested that a charging model for international tourists "would align the UK with other countries, such as New Zealand and Singapore".
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: On Tuesday, DCMS confirmed free admission to these museums would remain in place for everyone.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: "The government believes that charging overseas visitors could deter domestic visitors and that the impacts and benefits of charging would not be felt equally across the sector and therefore will not introduce charges for overseas visitors," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: Culture secretary Lisa Nandy said: "Our museums are the places that light up the world.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: "That's why they must be free, forever, for everyone to access." sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: Audio firm Taction Technology claimed in 2021 that Apple had infringed two of its patents for haptics systems, which enable vibrations for actions such as receiving a message or pressing a button.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: This tech is built into devices like the iPhone and Apple Watch.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: "While we thank the jury for their consideration, we strongly disagree with today's verdict and the damages awarded, which are entirely unsupported by the facts," it said.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: "Apple's Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction's technology, which Taction's own testing of Apple's products confirmed during trial." Haptics allow people to interact with devices by simulating the sense of touch or feel through vibrations.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: They have become a hallmark of modern devices, with smartphones, watches and video game controllers among those containing small motors that move in response to specific electronic signals.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: Apple's "Taptic Engine" system - enabling haptic feedback in its devices - first debuted with the Apple Watch in 2014.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: Taction, which makes headphones and gaming headsets, claimed in 2021 that these improvements infringed patents it was issued in 2020.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: It wrote in its complaint , external that by producing better haptic vibrations in its devices, Apple had been able to improve its overall user experience.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: It also accused Apple of using its inventions "without license or authority".
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: City have been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period, though they continue to deny any wrongdoing and have until 2 October to submit an appeal.
sentences.article_title: Infantino should have no place in future of football - Pinto

sentences.text: The Premier League investigation was launched following information released into the public domain by the Football Leaks website in 2018, via German publication Der Spiegel, and following a separate investigation by European football's governing body Uefa.

sentences.text: In a message on X , external , Rui Pinto, creator of Football Leaks, repeated allegations from 2018 that Infantino intervened to help City and Paris St-Germain avoid financial fair play sanctions from European football's governing body Uefa.
sentences.article_title: Infantino should have no place in future of football - Pinto

sentences.text: According to a report by Der Spiegel , external , the clubs overvalued sponsorship deals to help meet FFP rules and, when facing sanctions over the matter, the allegations in the documents state Infantino helped arrange more lenient punishments for them in 2014.
sentences.article_title: Infantino should have no place in future of football - Pinto

sentences.text: A PSG statement at the time said it "has always acted in full compliance with the laws and regulations enacted by sports institutions" and it "denies the allegations".
sentences.article_title: Infantino should have no place in future of football - Pinto

sentences.text: "Since the introduction of Financial Fair Play, Paris St-Germain have been one of the most audited and scrutinised clubs in history," the club added.
sentences.article_title: Infantino should have no place in future of football - Pinto

sentences.article_title: Infantino should have no place in future of football - Pinto

sentences.text: "All of these details were also revealed through Football Leaks.
sentences.article_title: Infantino should have no place in future of football - Pinto
